items.findings: This retrospective Phase-G review records the compliance level non_conformant for T4 under the standing delegation `01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14`. It names the four findings this batch admitted, each by id and by what is missing. v1-p6-2 (P1) — the systemic path terminates at a process-run id: `coach.rs:994-999` starts `KATA_PROCESS` with `{interruption_id}` and stores the run id as `kata_candidate_id`; there is no kata record naming an instrument and success threshold, no tenant-kata scoping, no measurement and no adoption gate, so a systemic finding never changes production. v1-p6-4 (P1) — interruptions are silently dropped: the cap counts every interruption on a card regardless of signature (`count_interruptions_for_card_tx`, line 603), refuses the fourth failed run at `COACH_INTERRUPTION_MAX` (line 608) with no coach card and no escalation, and `board/pull.rs:359` suppresses coaching whenever any live root run exists on the card. v1-p6-5 (P1) — the coach is wired only to failed runs: `coach.interrupt` has one caller, `err.card` (`board/pull.rs:424`); WIP breaches, stale leases, gate timeouts and board events, all section 6.2 inputs, have no producer. v1-p6-6 (P2) — orphan coach cards can be created by the public create path: `board/cards.rs:104` accepts any catalogue card type, including coach, and validates neither an interruption row nor `meta.interrupted_card_id`. Clause dispositions. Clause 2 is proved by `coach.rs::a_repeat_signature_escalates_instead_of_a_second_card` (line 683) and clause 3 by `::a_failed_coach_run_never_opens_a_coach_card` (line 745) with `::a_nested_coach_run_is_refused` (line 1343). Clause 1 has a named passing test for a first interruption (`::an_interruption_yields_one_coach_card_one_triage_and_one_remedy`, line 577) but is refuted as a universal by v1-p6-4, so it is not proved at HEAD. Clause 4 has a named passing test (`::a_systemic_class_opens_one_kata`, line 816, with `::a_transient_class_opens_no_kata`, line 864) but proves only a process start; v1-p6-2 shows the kata record, instrument and threshold that the clause intends are absent, so the clause is proved only in the weaker sense. This retrospective Phase-G review records the compliance level non_conformant for T2 under the standing delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14. It names the six findings this batch admitted, each by id and by what is missing. v1-t2-1 (P0) — a generated draft can be attached by `documents.compose` with no gate: the action accepts `card_id` and `meta.generated = true` and writes an attached, active document; the `draft.apply` gate exists only in `ladder.apply_draft` and the generated-class refusal only in `documents.update`, so the create path bypasses both. This finding blocks closure of the fourth §12 clause, "a generated draft cannot transition a card", and therefore blocks closure of T2. v1-t2-2 — L1 never calls laya: `ladder.evaluate` records the `answer`, `confidence`, `probabilities` and `latency_ms` supplied by its caller; `laya_configs` pins model_ref, params and timeout_ms, but no T2 path issues `POST /v1/systemone`, so the recorded L1 decision is a shape, not an inference. v1-t2-3 — `refinements.publish` is ungated: the action writes the tenant's threshold, rule and fail-action override and bumps its version with `confirm = "none"` and no approval, although §7.2 calls a refinement change a gated policy change; `decision_policies.update` is likewise ungated. v1-t2-4 — options and questions are inline free text: `ladder.evaluate` accepts an `options` array of key/label/payload objects and a free `question` string in the request, and `decision_policy` carries kind, gate, threshold, fail_policy and action but no authored question, `fire_when` or `min_confidence`, so §7.2's "options are rows, questions are rows" is not met. v1-t2-5 — budget code spelling: §7.5 records `429 budget_exceeded`, but T2 enforces no inference budget and the only budget refusal in the tree is the tool-spend `429 tool_budget_exceeded` in `crates/actions/src/invoke.rs` and `crates/actions/src/broker.rs` (#526), so the documented slug has no implementation. v1-t2-6 — a human decision cites any approved approval, not its gate: `ladder.record` calls `human_approved_gate_tx(..., None, card_id)`, so the `gate` it was given is never compared with `approval.gate`; only `ladder.apply_draft` passes `Some(DRAFT_APPLY_GATE)`, and a `gate.precheck` decision can cite an approval for a different gate on the same card.
